title: What Is a Plugged Well? | CAPIT Data Context
description: Learn what constitutes an officially plugged well under state regulatory guidelines and how CAPIT verifies record status.
headline: What Is a Plugged Well?
body: A plugged well is an inactive oil or gas well that a state regulatory agency confirms has been permanently sealed downhole with cement and restored at the surface to prevent environmental fluid migration and groundwater contamination.

sections.heading: State Status Language
sections.body: State agencies use specific terminology to represent completed plugging operations (e.g., 'Plugged & Abandoned', 'P&A Completed', or 'Approved Plugging Report'). CAPIT retains the original state status alongside normalized display labels.
